name: cp
description: Copies a SOURCE to a DESTINATION, or several sources into a directory. If the destination already exists, it is overwritten without confirmation, unless -i or -n is used.

options.description: Copies directories and everything in them. Required to copy a folder. -R is the same.
Asks for confirmation before overwriting an existing file.
Preserves the files’ mode, owner and timestamps.
Archive mode: a recursive copy that preserves everything (links, permissions, timestamps). Same as -dR --preserve=all.
Copies only if the source is newer than the destination, or if the destination does not exist.
Creates hard links instead of copying.
Creates symbolic links instead of copying.
Copies every source into this directory.

arguments.name: DESTINATION
arguments.description: New file name, or directory to put the copies in.

examples.explanation: Makes a copy of report.txt named report.bak.
Copies the project directory and everything in it.
Copies the JPEG images to ~/Pictures, asking before overwriting and printing each copy.
An exact backup of a configuration (permissions and timestamps kept).

dangerNote: cp overwrites the destination without warning if it already exists. Add -i to be warned.
